custodian_intel.details:
• Edward Jones is traditional — if the account titles don't match exactly between the delivering and receiving accounts, they'll reject the ACAT and force a manual LOA. Double-check registration/titling before you submit
  • EJ frequently holds proprietary "Bridge Builder" funds that can't be held anywhere else — those must be liquidated before/at transfer, they won't come over in kind. Scan the holdings for them up front and set client expectations if any are present.
custodian_intel.contact_info: Signature: DocuSign OK. Medallion: Not required. Letter of acceptance: Not required. Paperwork returned by: N/A for a standard ACAT

custodian_intel.details: Fidelity managed accounts auto-liquidate. If the client is in Fidelity Premium Services, Portfolio Advisory Services, or Wealth Services, the proprietary funds in those sleeves automatically liquidate during a full ACAT — no separate liquidation paperwork needed. But for a Non-IRA client that's a taxable event, so the standard disclaimer applies — set that expectation before you pull the transfer. A plain Fidelity retail brokerage account, by contrast, just comes over in kind.

custodian_intel.details:
• BNY requires its own IRA transfer forms, plus Schwab-omnibus routing as the client’s receiving number
  • Fund side: DTC = 5523
  • Pershing side: DTC = 0443

custodian_intel.details:
• Clears through Pershing
  • Apex signs the paperwork — the LOA needs Apex's own signature as successor custodian; get it from Apex before submitting.
  • Liquidates even on in-kind requests — don't count on shares coming over; plan for cash.
  • Fast once processed — the delay is getting the paperwork right, not TRP's processing time.
